artworks.title: Tiresias Transformed into a Woman
artworks.description: Della Vecchia's Tiresias transformed into a woman — the snake-strike that begins the quarrel of Hera and Zeus and ends in blindness.

artworks.title: Manto and Tiresias
artworks.description: Singleton's Manto and Tiresias — the blind seer led by his daughter, sight traded for prophetic knowledge.

artworks.title: Teiresias Foretells the Future to Odysseus
artworks.description: Fuseli's Teiresias before Odysseus — the sightless prophet whose underworld voice still guides the living.

artworks.title: Odysseus Takes Counsel with Teiresias
artworks.description: Abildgaard's Odysseus taking counsel with Teiresias — the blind shade of the Nekyia.

popCulture.title: Metamorphoses
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Book III — the snakes, seven years as a woman, Hera's blinding, and Zeus' gift of prophecy that outlives sight.

popCulture.title: The Waste Land
popCulture.creator: T. S. Eliot
popCulture.description: Eliot's blind seer watches the modern city — Tiresias as the poem's dual-sexed witness to sterility and desire.

popCulture.title: Tiresias
popCulture.description: The Theban prophet who saw both sexes remains the name for insight bought by blindness.
